caption:
Mountain biking in Costa Rica eventually teaches every rider the same lesson: some slopes are meant to be walked. When the gradient crosses thirty percent on wet grass, pushing your bike isn't a defeat—it's strategy. In the highlands, old farming tracks cut straight up the ridges rather than contouring around them. It saves space for pasture, but it means the climbs are uncompromisingly direct. You learn to listen to your lungs, step over the wet clay, and look up at the canopy. Which climb has made you step off the saddle?
